title.en: Volume 378 Biographies 165: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, Zhu Qi

sentences.zh: 列傳一百六十五

translations.literal: Biographies 165
translations.idiomatic: Biography 165

sentences.zh: 黃爵滋金應麟陳慶鏞蘇廷魁朱琦

translations.literal: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, Zhu Qi
translations.idiomatic: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi

sentences.zh: 黃爵滋，字樹齋，江西宜黃人。

translations.literal: Huang Juezi, style name Shuzhai, was a native of Yihuang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Juezi, whose style was Shuzhai, came from Yihuang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 道光三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史、給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Daoguang reign he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and was promoted to censor and supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the third year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, served as a compiler, and rose to censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 以直諫負時望，遇事鋒發，無所迴避，言屢被採納。

translations.literal: He enjoyed a reputation for forthright remonstrance; on every matter he struck sharply and shrank from nothing, and his words were repeatedly adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for blunt remonstrance, spoke out sharply on every issue without holding back, and the court often took his advice.

sentences.zh: 十五年，特擢鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was specially promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the reign he was specially promoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 詔以爵滋及科道中馮贊勳、金應麟、曾望顏諸人均敢言，故特加擢任，風勵言官，開忠諫之路，勉其勿因驟得升階，即圖保位，並以誥誡臣工焉。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because Juezi and among the supervising secretaries Feng Zanxun, Jin Yinglin, Zeng Wangyan, and others were all daring in speech, they were therefore specially promoted to encourage remonstrating officials, open the path of loyal counsel, urge them not because of sudden advancement to seek only to preserve their posts, and also to admonish the officials as a body.
translations.idiomatic: An edict explained that Juezi, Feng Zanxun, Jin Yinglin, Zeng Wangyan, and other outspoken supervising secretaries had been promoted specially to encourage remonstrating officials, open a path for loyal counsel, and warn them not to rest content with their new rank; the same edict admonished the bureaucracy at large.

sentences.zh: 尋疏陳察天道，廣言路，儲將才，制匪民，整飭京城營衛，申嚴外夷防禁六事，又陳漕、河積弊，均下議行。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he memorialized on six matters: observing Heaven's way, broadening the avenue of speech, storing up military talent, controlling unruly commoners, rectifying the capital's garrison guards, and tightening defenses against foreigners; he also set forth accumulated abuses in grain transport and river control, all of which were sent down for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted memorials on six topics—reading Heaven's signs, widening channels of remonstrance, cultivating generals, restraining lawless commoners, reforming the capital garrisons, and tightening coastal defenses against foreigners—and on long-standing abuses in the Grand Canal and river works; the court ordered discussion and implementation of each.

sentences.zh: 時英吉利船艦屢至閩、浙、江南、山東洋面遊奕，測繪山川地圖。

translations.literal: At the time English ships repeatedly came to cruise the seas off Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong, surveying mountains, rivers, and maps.
translations.idiomatic: English vessels were then repeatedly cruising the coasts of Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong, surveying terrain and charting maps.

sentences.zh: 爵滋疏言：「外國不可盡以恩撫，而沿海無備可危。

translations.literal: Juezi memorialized, saying: "Foreign states cannot all be treated entirely with gracious appeasement, and the coast being unprepared is perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi wrote: "Foreign powers cannot all be won over by kindness alone, and our undefended coast is in real danger.

sentences.zh: 」十八年，上禁煙議疏曰：「竊見近年銀價遞增，每銀一兩，易制錢一千六百有零，非耗銀於內地，實漏銀於外洋也。

translations.literal: " In the eighteenth year he submitted a memorial on prohibiting opium, saying: "Your servant observes that in recent years the price of silver has risen steadily; for each tael of silver one receives more than sixteen hundred cash in standard coin. This is not silver being consumed within the interior, but silver actually leaking to the outer seas.
translations.idiomatic: " In the eighteenth year he submitted his famous memorial urging prohibition of opium: "Your servant observes that silver has grown dearer year by year—each tael now exchanges for more than sixteen hundred cash. The drain is not domestic waste but silver flowing out to foreign seas.

sentences.zh: 蓋自鴉片流入中國，道光三年以前，每歲漏銀數百萬兩，其初不過紈褲子弟習為浮靡。

translations.literal: This is because since opium flowed into China, before the third year of Daoguang several million taels leaked out each year; at first it was only the sons of silk-trousered families who took it up as a dissolute fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Since opium entered China, several million taels had been lost annually even before the third year of Daoguang, when only pampered sons of the gentry took it up as fashionable excess.

sentences.zh: 嗣後上自官府搢紳，下至工商優隸，以及婦女僧道，隨在吸食。

translations.literal: Afterward, from officials and gentry above down to artisans, merchants, actors, and bond servants below, as well as women, monks, and Taoist priests, all smoked wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: Soon officials and gentry at the top, artisans, merchants, actors, and servants below, and even women, monks, and priests were smoking everywhere.

sentences.zh: 粵省奸商勾通兵弁，用扒龍、快蟹等船，運銀出洋，運煙入口。

translations.literal: Wicked merchants of Guangdong province colluded with military clerks, using luggers, fast crabs, and other vessels to transport silver out to sea and opium into port.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong merchants colluded with garrison clerks, using luggers, fast crabs, and similar craft to ship silver abroad and opium ashore.

sentences.zh: 故自道光三年至十一年，歲漏銀一千七八百萬兩；

translations.literal: Therefore from the third year of Daoguang to the eleventh, seventeen or eighteen million taels leaked out each year;
translations.idiomatic: From the third year of Daoguang through the eleventh, seventeen or eighteen million taels leaked out yearly;

sentences.zh: 十一年至十四年，歲漏銀二千餘萬兩；

translations.literal: from the eleventh to the fourteenth, more than twenty million taels each year;
translations.idiomatic: from the eleventh through the fourteenth, more than twenty million taels a year;

sentences.zh: 十四年至今，漸漏至三千萬之多；

translations.literal: from the fourteenth year to the present it has gradually reached more than thirty million;
translations.idiomatic: and since the fourteenth year the annual loss has climbed toward thirty million;

sentences.zh: 福建、浙江、山東、天津各海口合之亦數千萬兩。

translations.literal: the ports of Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, and Tianjin together also amount to tens of millions of taels.
translations.idiomatic: while Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, and Tianjin ports together account for tens of millions more.

sentences.zh: 以中土有用之財，填海外無窮之壑，易此害人之物，漸成病國之憂，年復一年，不知伊於胡底。

translations.literal: Using the useful wealth of the Central Land to fill the bottomless gulf beyond the seas, exchanging this thing that harms men, it has gradually become a worry that sickens the state, year after year, with no knowing where it will end.
translations.idiomatic: China's useful wealth pours into a bottomless foreign abyss in exchange for a substance that poisons men, and year by year the nation sickens with no end in sight.

sentences.zh: 各省州縣地丁錢糧，徵錢為多，及辦奏銷，以錢為銀，前此多有贏餘，今則無不賠貼。

translations.literal: In every province, prefecture, and county the land tax and grain levies are collected mostly in cash; when accounts are rendered for imperial approval, cash is converted to silver. Formerly there were often surpluses; now there is never a case without shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces collect land tax largely in cash and convert it to silver when reporting to the throne; accounts that once showed surpluses now always run short.

sentences.zh: 各省鹽商賣鹽得錢，交課用銀，昔之爭為利藪者，今則視為畏途。

translations.literal: In every province salt merchants sell salt for cash and pay duties in silver; what was once fiercely contested as a source of profit is now regarded as a road of dread.
translations.idiomatic: Salt merchants who once fought for lucrative franchises now treat their trade as a path to ruin, for they must pay duties in silver from cash receipts.

sentences.zh: 若再數年，銀價愈貴，奏銷如何能辦？

translations.literal: If for several more years silver grows dearer, how can accounts for imperial approval be settled?
translations.idiomatic: If silver grows dearer for a few more years, how will the court settle its accounts?

sentences.zh: 積課如何能清？

translations.literal: How can accumulated tax arrears be cleared?
translations.idiomatic: How will accumulated tax arrears ever be cleared?

sentences.zh: 設有不測之用，又如何能支？

translations.literal: If there should be unforeseen expenditures, how could they be met?
translations.idiomatic: If an emergency arose, how could the treasury meet it?

sentences.zh: 今天下皆知漏卮在鴉片，而未知所以禁也。

translations.literal: Today all under Heaven know the leaking vessel is opium, yet do not know how to prohibit it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows opium is the leak, yet no one knows how to stop it.

sentences.zh: 夫耗銀之多，由於販煙之盛；

translations.literal: The great consumption of silver comes from the flourishing of opium trafficking;
translations.idiomatic: Silver drains away because the opium trade flourishes;

sentences.zh: 販煙之盛，由於食煙之眾。

translations.literal: the flourishing of trafficking comes from the multitude of smokers.
translations.idiomatic: and trafficking flourishes because smokers are so numerous.

sentences.zh: 無吸食自無興販，無興販則外洋之煙自不來矣。

translations.literal: Without smoking there would naturally be no trafficking; without trafficking the opium of the outer seas would naturally not come.
translations.idiomatic: Without smokers there would be no traffickers, and without traffickers foreign opium would not enter.

sentences.zh: 宜先重治吸食，臣請皇上准給一年期限戒菸，雖至深之癮，未有不能斷絕者。

translations.literal: One should first punish smoking heavily. Your servant asks Your Majesty to grant a one-year term to quit smoking; even the deepest addiction has none who cannot break it.
translations.idiomatic: Smoking should be punished first and severely. Your servant asks that smokers be given one year to quit; even the deepest addiction can be broken.

sentences.zh: 至一年仍然服食，是不奉法之亂民，加之重刑不足卹。

translations.literal: If after one year they still consume, they are lawless rebels who do not obey the statutes, and imposing heavy punishment would not be excessive pity.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone still smoking after a year would be a rebel defying the law, and the heaviest penalty would be no more than they deserve.

sentences.zh: 舊例吸煙罪止枷杖，其不指出興販者，罪止杖一百、徒三年，俱系活罪。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations the crime of smoking opium was only cangue and beating; for those who did not denounce traffickers the penalty was only one hundred blows and three years' penal servitude—all punishments sparing life.
translations.idiomatic: Under old law smoking brought only the cangue or the rod, and failure to denounce traffickers brought a hundred blows and three years' servitude—all punishments that spared life.

sentences.zh: 斷癮之苦，甚於枷杖與徒，故不肯斷絕。

translations.literal: The suffering of breaking the addiction is worse than cangue, beating, and servitude, so they are unwilling to break off.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawal hurts more than the cangue or exile, so addicts refuse to quit.

sentences.zh: 若罪以死論，臨刑之慘急，苦於斷癮之苟延，臣知其原死於家而不原死於市。

translations.literal: If the crime were judged by death, the agony and urgency at the moment of execution would be more bitter than the lingering pain of breaking the addiction; your servant knows they would rather die at home than die in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Make the crime capital, and the terror of execution would outweigh the pain of withdrawal; your servant knows they would rather die at home than on the scaffold.

sentences.zh: 況我皇上​​雷霆之威，赫然震怒，雖愚頑沉溺之久，自足以發聾振瞶。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty's thunderbolt authority, manifest in blazing wrath, would of itself suffice to deafen the ears and startle the eyes, even of those long sunk in folly and addiction.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty's thunderous wrath would startle even the most stubborn long-term addict into sobriety.

sentences.zh: 皇上之旨嚴，則奉法之吏肅，犯法之人畏。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's orders are strict, the officials who uphold the law are stern, and those who violate the law are in awe.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne's orders are strict, enforcing officials grow stern and lawbreakers grow afraid.

sentences.zh: 一年之內，尚未用刑，十已戒其八九。

translations.literal: Within one year, before punishments have even been applied, eight or nine out of ten will already have quit.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year, before a single execution, eight or nine in ten will have quit on their own.

sentences.zh: 已食者藉國法以保餘生，未食者因炯戒以全身命，止闢之大權，即好生之盛德也。

translations.literal: Those who have smoked would rely on the state's law to preserve the remainder of their lives; those who have not smoked would through stern warning preserve body and life; the great authority to stop and prohibit is itself the abundant virtue of cherishing life.
translations.idiomatic: Former smokers would owe their lives to the law, and those who never smoked would be warned away; the power to prohibit is itself the throne's mercy.

sentences.zh: 伏請飭諭各督撫嚴行清查保甲，初先曉諭，定於一年後取具五家互結，準令舉發，給予優獎。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly asks that each governor-general and governor be ordered strictly to investigate the baojia system, first instructing the people, fixing that after one year five-house mutual bonds be obtained, allowing denunciation, and granting generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly asks that governors-general and governors be ordered to enforce the baojia system strictly: first instruct the people, then after one year require five-house mutual bonds, allow denunciation, and grant generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 倘有容隱，本犯照新例處死，互結之家照例治罪。

translations.literal: If there is concealment, the principal offender shall be executed according to the new regulations, and the households of the mutual bond shall be punished according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Concealment would bring execution under the new statute for the offender and punishment for every household in the mutual bond.

sentences.zh: 通都大邑，往來客商，責成店鋪，如有容留食煙之人，照窩藏匪類治罪。

translations.literal: In great thoroughfares and large cities, for traveling merchants coming and going, shops shall be held responsible; if they harbor smokers, they shall be punished as for concealing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In major cities, inns and shops that harbor traveling smokers shall be punished as for sheltering bandits.

sentences.zh: 文武大小各官，照常人加等，子孫不准考試。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials great and small shall receive punishment one degree heavier than commoners, and their descendants shall not be permitted to sit examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of every rank would face penalties one degree heavier than commoners, and their descendants would be barred from examinations.

sentences.zh: 官親幕友家丁，除本犯治罪外，本管官嚴加議處。

translations.literal: Officials' kin, secretaries, and household servants, besides punishing the principal offender, shall have the supervising official severely deliberated for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' relatives, secretaries, and servants would be punished, and their supervising officials would face severe disciplinary review.

sentences.zh: 滿、漢官兵，照地方官保甲辦理；

translations.literal: Manchu and Han officers and soldiers shall be handled according to the baojia procedures of local officials;
translations.idiomatic: Manchu and Han troops would be handled under the same baojia rules as civilians;

sentences.zh: 管轄失察之人，照地方官辦理。

translations.literal: those in jurisdiction who failed to detect shall be handled as local officials are handled.
translations.idiomatic: and officers who failed to detect offenders would be punished like negligent local officials.

sentences.zh: 庶幾軍民一體，上下肅清，漏卮可塞，銀價不至再昂，然後講求理財之方，誠天下萬世臣民之福也。

translations.literal: Then perhaps army and people would be one body, above and below purified, the leaking vessel could be stopped, and the price of silver would not rise again; only then could methods of managing state finances be pursued—truly the blessing of all under Heaven for ten thousand generations of subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Thus army and people alike would be cleansed, the leak stopped, and silver stabilized; only then could fiscal reform proceed—truly a blessing for the empire and its people for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，上深韙之，下疆臣各抒所見，速議章程。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up, the Emperor deeply approved it and sent it down for frontier officials each to set forth their views and quickly deliberate regulations.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor strongly approved the memorial and ordered frontier officials to submit opinions and draft regulations at once.

sentences.zh: 先是，太常寺少卿許乃濟疏言，煙禁雖嚴，閉關不可，徒法不行，請仍用舊制納稅，以貨易貨，不得用銀購買，吸食罪名，專重官員、士子、兵丁，時皆謂非政體。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xu Naiji had memorialized that although the opium ban was strict, closing the ports was impossible and empty law would not be enforced; he asked to restore the old system of paying tax, bartering goods for goods, not permitting purchase with silver, and making the crime of smoking apply especially to officials, scholars, and soldiers—at the time all said this was not proper statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Naiji of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had argued that strict prohibition was futile while ports stayed closed, and proposed legalizing opium under the old tax system with barter instead of silver and heavier penalties only for officials, scholars, and soldiers—a plan widely condemned as unsound policy.

sentences.zh: 爵滋劾乃濟，罷其職，連擢爵滋大理寺少卿、通政使、禮部侍郎，調刑部。

translations.literal: Juezi impeached Naiji and had him dismissed; Juezi was then continuously promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, Commissioner of the Office of Transmission, Vice Minister of Rites, and transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi impeached Xu Naiji and had him dismissed, then rose in quick succession to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, transmission commissioner, vice minister of Rites, and finally the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 十九年，廷臣議定販煙、吸煙罪名新例，略如爵滋所請。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the court officials deliberated and fixed new regulations for the crimes of trafficking and smoking opium, broadly as Juezi had requested.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year the court enacted new penalties for trafficking and smoking opium, largely along the lines Juezi had proposed.

sentences.zh: 林則徐至粵，盡焚躉船存煙，議外國人販煙罪。

translations.literal: Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong, burned all the opium stored on receiving ships, and deliberated the crime of foreigners trafficking opium.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Zexu reached Guangdong he burned all opium held on receiving ships and pressed charges against foreign traffickers.

sentences.zh: 英領事義律不就約束，兵釁遂開。

translations.literal: The English consul Elliot would not submit to restraint, and military hostilities thus opened.
translations.idiomatic: The British consul Charles Elliot refused to submit, and hostilities broke out.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命爵滋偕左都御史祁俊藻赴福建查辦禁煙，與總督鄧廷楨籌備海防。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Juezi was ordered together with Left Censor-in-Chief Qi Junzao to go to Fujian to investigate and handle opium prohibition, and with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen to plan coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Juezi and Left Censor-in-Chief Qi Junzao were sent to Fujian to oversee prohibition and, with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen, to plan coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 洎英兵來犯，廷楨屢挫敵於廈門，上疑之。

translations.literal: When English troops came to attack, Tingzhen repeatedly defeated the enemy at Xiamen, but the Emperor was suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When British forces attacked, Deng Tingzhen claimed repeated victories at Xiamen, but the Emperor grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 爵滋與俊藻方至浙江按事，復命赴福建察奏。

translations.literal: Juezi and Junzao had just reached Zhejiang to conduct investigations when they were again ordered to go to Fujian to inspect and report.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi and Qi Junzao were investigating in Zhejiang when they were ordered to Fujian to report.

sentences.zh: 疏陳：「廷楨所奏不誣；

translations.literal: They memorialized: "What Tingzhen reported is not false;
translations.idiomatic: They reported: "Deng Tingzhen's accounts were not false;

sentences.zh: 定海不可不速復；

translations.literal: Dinghai cannot but be quickly recovered;
translations.idiomatic: Dinghai must be recovered quickly;

sentences.zh: 水師有專門之技，宜破格用人。

translations.literal: the naval forces have specialized skills, and one should break precedent in employing men.
translations.idiomatic: the navy has specialized skills and men should be appointed outside normal seniority rules.

sentences.zh: 」具言戰守方略。

translations.literal: " They set forth in detail strategies for fighting and defense.
translations.idiomatic: " They laid out detailed strategies for offense and defense.

sentences.zh: 又言浙江為閩、粵之心腹，與江蘇為脣齒，請飭伊里布不可偏聽琦善，信敵必退。

translations.literal: They also said Zhejiang was the heart and belly of Fujian and Guangdong, and with Jiangsu was lip and teeth; they asked that Yilibu be instructed not to listen one-sidedly to Qishan and believe the enemy would certainly withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: They warned that Zhejiang was the strategic heart of Fujian and Guangdong and closely linked to Jiangsu, and urged that Yilibu not heed Qishan alone or assume the enemy would withdraw.

sentences.zh: 及回京，復極言英人勞師襲遠不足慮，宜竟與絕市，募兵節餉，為持久計，以海防圖進。

translations.literal: When they returned to the capital they again spoke forcefully that English troops worn by distant campaigns were not to be feared, that trade should simply be cut off, troops recruited and expenditures economized for a long-term plan, and presented a coastal defense map.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital they argued that overstretched British forces were no serious threat, urged a complete trade embargo, recruitment, and fiscal austerity for a long war, and submitted a coastal defense map.

sentences.zh: 既而琦善在粵議撫不得要領，連歲命將出師，廣東、浙江皆不利。

translations.literal: Before long Qishan's negotiations for appeasement in Guangdong failed to grasp essentials; year after year generals were ordered to take the field, and in both Guangdong and Zhejiang the situation was unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Qishan's appeasement talks in Guangdong then collapsed, and year after year campaigns in Guangdong and Zhejiang went badly.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，英兵由海入江，乃定和議於江寧，煙禁自此弛矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year English troops entered the Yangzi from the sea, and peace was settled at Jiangning; from this the opium ban was relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year British forces advanced up the Yangzi, peace was made at Nanjing, and opium prohibition was effectively abandoned.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂去官。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he left office on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 爵滋為御史時，稽察戶部銀庫，嘗疏言庫丁輕收虧帑之弊。

translations.literal: When Juezi was a censor he inspected the Board of Revenue silver vault and once memorialized on the abuse of vault clerks taking light receipts and causing treasury shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: As a censor he had inspected the Board of Revenue silver vault and warned of clerks who accepted light payments and caused shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，銀庫虧空九百萬兩事發，追論管庫、查庫諸臣，罪皆褫職責賠，賠既足，次第予官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the matter of a nine-million-tael shortfall in the silver vault broke out; officials who managed and inspected the vault were pursued, all were stripped of office and ordered to compensate; when compensation was complete they were gradually given offices again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year a nine-million-tael vault shortfall was exposed; vault managers and inspectors were stripped of rank and ordered to pay restitution, and were gradually reappointed once they had paid in full.

sentences.zh: 爵滋以員外郎候補，病足家居，上猶時問其何在。

translations.literal: Juezi awaited appointment as an outside-section vice director; ill in the feet he remained at home, yet the Emperor still sometimes asked where he was.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi awaited appointment as an outside-section vice director but stayed home with a foot ailment; the Emperor still occasionally asked after him.

sentences.zh: 三十年，至京，會上崩，遂不出。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he reached the capital; it happened that the Emperor died, and he therefore did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he reached the capital just as the Emperor died, and he never took office again.

sentences.zh: 逾三年，卒。

translations.literal: After more than three years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died three years later.

sentences.zh: 爵滋以詩名，喜交遊，每夜閉閣草奏，日騎出，遍視諸故人名士，飲酒賦詩，意氣豪甚。

translations.literal: Juezi was famous for poetry and loved socializing; each night he closed his study to draft memorials, and by day rode out to visit all his old friends and eminent men, drinking wine and composing verse, his spirit very bold.
translations.idiomatic: Juezi was known for poetry and loved company; he drafted memorials by night and rode out by day to visit friends and luminaries, drinking and composing verse with great bravado.

sentences.zh: 及創議禁煙，始終主戰，一時以為清流眉目。

translations.literal: When he initiated the proposal to prohibit opium he always advocated war, and for a time was regarded as the leading figure of the moralist faction.
translations.idiomatic: When he launched the drive to prohibit opium he consistently favored war and was seen for a time as the moral leader of the Qingliu faction.

sentences.zh: 所著奏議、詩文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected memorials and poetry circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials and collected poems circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 金應麟，字亞伯，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Jin Yinglin, style name Yabo, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yinglin, whose style was Yabo, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以舉人入貲為中書。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased office and became a secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he purchased appointment as a Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，成進士，授刑部主事，總辦秋審，先後從大臣讞獄四川、湖北、山西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, supervised the autumn assizes, and successively followed great ministers in reviewing cases in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the sixth year of Daoguang, served as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, supervised the autumn assizes, and accompanied senior officials on judicial reviews in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 累擢郎中，改御史，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director, changed to censor, and moved to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director, then censor, then supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏請修改刑例，於鬥毆、報盜、劫囚、誣告、私鑄、服舍違式、斷罪引律、奴婢毆主、故禁故勘平人、應捕人追捕罪人、犯罪存留養親、官司出入人罪、徒流遷徙地方、外省駐防逃人，逐條論列，多被採取改定；

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting revision of the penal code, setting forth article by article on brawling, reporting bandits, rescuing prisoners, false accusation, private coining, violation of mourning dress and dwelling regulations, citing statutes in sentencing, slaves and maids beating masters, wrongful imprisonment and torture of commoners, authorized pursuers chasing criminals, crimes with retention to support parents, officials improperly releasing or admitting guilt, places of exile for penal servitude and banishment, and fugitives from garrisons in outer provinces—many were adopted and revised;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for revision of the penal code, discussing brawling, bandit reports, prison breaks, false accusation, private coining, mourning violations, sentencing citations, slave assaults on masters, wrongful imprisonment, authorized pursuit, crimes with parental support exemptions, official misconduct in sentencing, exile destinations, and garrison fugitives—many of his proposals were adopted;

sentences.zh: 又論銅船恣橫不法及驛站擾累諸弊，並下各省督撫禁革。

translations.literal: he also discussed the lawlessness of copper transport boats running rampant and the abuses of postal stations causing hardship, all sent down to governors-general and governors of every province to prohibit and abolish.
translations.idiomatic: he also denounced abuses by copper transport boats and postal stations, and orders went to every province to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 先後封事數十上，劾疆臣琦善、河臣吳邦慶尤為時稱。

translations.literal: He submitted sealed memorials several tens in succession; his impeachments of frontier official Qishan and river official Wu Bangqing were especially praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted dozens of sealed memorials; his impeachments of Qishan and river official Wu Bangqing won particular praise.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘉其敢言，擢太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor commended his daring speech and promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor praised his outspokenness and promoted him to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 遭憂歸，服闋，授鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: He returned on mourning, and when mourning ended was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for mourning and, when it ended, was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 疏論水師廢弛，漕政頹紊。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the naval forces being lax and decayed and grain transport administration being decadent and disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the decay of the navy and the disorder of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出為直隸按察使，鞫護理長蘆鹽運使楊成業等得贓獄，論遣戍，前運使陳崇禮等並罣議。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as surveillance commissioner of Zhili, tried acting Changlu salt transport commissioner Yang Chengye and others in a bribery case, sentenced them to banishment, and former transport commissioner Chen Chongli and others were also implicated.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became surveillance commissioner of Zhili, tried acting Changlu salt commissioner Yang Chengye and others for bribery, sentenced them to exile, and implicated former commissioner Chen Chongli.

sentences.zh: 尋召為大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was recalled as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，疏言：「海疆諸臣欺罔，其故由於爵祿之念重，而趨避之計工。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he memorialized: "Coastal officials deceive and mislead; the reason is that thoughts of rank and salary weigh heavily, while schemes of evasion and avoidance are finely wrought.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he wrote: "Coastal officials deceive the throne because they prize rank and salary and excel at evasion.

sentences.zh: 欲破其欺，是在乾斷。

translations.literal: To break their deception lies in resolute decision.
translations.idiomatic: To break their deceit requires resolute imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 資格不可拘，嫌疑不必避，舊過不妨宥，重賞不宜惜。

translations.literal: Seniority must not be rigidly held to, suspicion need not be avoided, old faults may be pardoned, and heavy rewards should not be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Do not bind yourself to seniority, do not shun the suspect, pardon past faults, and spare no reward.

sentences.zh: 近頃長江海口鎮兵足守，而敵船深入，逃潰時聞。

translations.literal: Recently at the Yangzi estuary garrison troops were sufficient to defend, yet enemy ships penetrated deeply, and flight and rout were heard from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Recently at the Yangzi estuary ample garrison troops were on hand, yet enemy ships penetrated deep inland and rout was reported again and again.

sentences.zh: 竭億萬氓庶之脂膏。

translations.literal: They exhaust the fat and cream of hundreds of millions of common people.
translations.idiomatic: They exhaust the substance of millions of common people

sentences.zh: 保一二庸臣之軀命。

translations.literal: to preserve the bodies and lives of one or two mediocre officials.
translations.idiomatic: to preserve the lives of one or two mediocre officials.

sentences.zh: 議者諉謂無人無兵無餉無械。

translations.literal: Those who deliberated shifted blame, saying there were no men, no troops, no funds, no weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Councillors shift blame, claiming there are no men, no troops, no funds, and no weapons.

sentences.zh: 竊以無人當求，無兵當練，無餉械亦當計度固有，多則持重，少則用謀，作三軍之氣，定邊疆之危，在皇上假以事權，與任事者運用一心而已。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that if there are no men one should seek them, if there are no troops one should train them; if there are no funds and weapons one should still calculate what is inherently available—if many, hold firm; if few, use stratagem; rouse the spirit of the three armies and settle the peril of the frontier borders—it rests only on Your Majesty granting authority for affairs and the responsible officials applying their minds as one.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that men must be sought, troops trained, and whatever funds and arms exist must be counted; with many, stand firm; with few, use stratagem; rouse the armies and secure the frontier—it requires only that Your Majesty delegate full authority and that responsible officials act in concert.

sentences.zh: 」复疏進預計度支圖、火器圖、籌海戰方略甚悉。

translations.literal: " He again memorialized, presenting advance budget charts, firearms charts, and coastal war plans in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: " He also submitted detailed advance budget charts, firearms diagrams, and coastal war plans.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以親老乞歸省，不復出。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, because his parents were aged he asked to return home to visit them and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he asked leave to care for aged parents and never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 著有廌華堂奏議及駢體文。

translations.literal: He authored the Zhihua Hall memorials and parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Zhihua Hall memorials and parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 陳慶鏞，字頌南，福建晉江人。

translations.literal: Chen Qingyong, style name Songnan, was a native of Jinjiang in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingyong, whose style was Songnan, came from Jinjiang in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，散館授戶部主事，遷員外郎，授御史。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the twelfth year of Daoguang, selected Hanlin bachelor, after leaving the academy appointed principal clerk in the Board of Revenue, promoted to outside-section vice director, appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the twelfth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy, then served in the Board of Revenue as principal clerk and outside-section vice director before becoming a censor.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，海疆僨事，獲罪諸臣浸復起用。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, when coastal affairs went awry, officials who had been punished were gradually reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, as coastal affairs worsened, officials who had been punished were gradually reappointed.

sentences.zh: 慶鏞上疏論刑賞失措，曰：「行政之要，莫大於刑賞。

translations.literal: Qingyong submitted a memorial on the misplacement of punishments and rewards, saying: "In administering government nothing is greater than punishments and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyong memorialized on misplaced punishments and rewards: "In government nothing matters more than punishments and rewards.

sentences.zh: 刑賞之權，操之於君，喻之於民，所以示天下之大公也。

translations.literal: The authority over punishments and rewards is wielded by the ruler and made known to the people—this is how the great impartiality of all under Heaven is shown.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler holds the power of punishment and reward and makes it known to the people—that is how the empire's impartiality is displayed.

sentences.zh: 大學論平天下之道，在於絜矩。

translations.literal: The Great Learning discusses the way to bring peace to the realm as lying in measuring the square.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Learning teaches that bringing peace to the realm depends on setting the measuring square.

sentences.zh: 矩者何，民之好惡是已。

translations.literal: What is the square? It is the people's likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: What is that square? The likes and dislikes of the people.

sentences.zh: 海疆多事以來，自總督、將軍以至州縣丞倅，禽駭獸奔。

translations.literal: Since coastal troubles multiplied, from governors-general and generals down to prefects, districts, and deputies, all fled like startled birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Since coastal troubles began, governors-general, generals, prefects, and deputies alike fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 皇上赫然震怒，失律之罪，法有莫逭。

translations.literal: The Emperor blazed in wrath, and the crime of violating military discipline admitted no escape under the law.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor blazed in wrath, and the law allowed no escape for those who had violated military discipline.

sentences.zh: 於是辱國之將軍奕山、奕經，參贊文蔚，總督牛鑑，提督餘步雲，先後就逮，步雲伏法。

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals who shamed the state, Yishan and Yijing, the staff officer Wenwei, Governor Niu Jian, and Provincial Commander Yu Buyun were successively arrested; Buyun was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The disgraced generals Yishan and Yijing, staff officer Wenwei, Governor Niu Jian, and Provincial Commander Yu Buyun were arrested in turn, and Buyun was executed.

sentences.zh: 血氣之倫，罔不拊手稱快，謂國法前雖未伸於琦善，今猶伸於餘步雲。

translations.literal: Men of spirit all clapped their hands in satisfaction, saying that though state law had not before been enforced on Qishan, it was now enforced on Yu Buyun.
translations.idiomatic: Men of spirit applauded, saying that though the law had not reached Qishan, it had at least reached Yu Buyun.

sentences.zh: 乃未幾起琦善為葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: Yet before long Qishan was reappointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before long Qishan was reappointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 邸報既傳，人情震駭，猶解之曰：'古聖王之待罪人，有投四裔以御魑魅者。

translations.literal: When the court gazette spread the news, the people were shaken with alarm; some still explained it, saying: "The ancient sage kings in dealing with criminals had those cast into the four borderlands to repel demons.
translations.idiomatic: When the court gazette spread the news, the public was appalled; some still explained it by saying, "Ancient sage kings cast criminals into the borderlands to repel demons.

sentences.zh: '皇上之於琦善，殆其類是，而今且以三品頂戴用為熱河都統矣，且用奕經為葉爾羌幫辦大臣，文蔚為古城領隊大臣矣。

translations.literal: " Your Majesty's treatment of Qishan is perhaps of that kind—yet now he is employed as Rehe commandant with third-rank insignia, Yijing is employed as Yarkand assistant commissioner, and Wenwei as Gucheng expedition leader.
translations.idiomatic: " Your Majesty's treatment of Qishan may be of that kind—yet now he serves as Rehe commandant with third-rank insignia, Yijing as Yarkand assistant commissioner, and Wenwei as Gucheng expedition leader.

sentences.zh: 琦善於戰事方始，首先示弱，以惰軍心，海內糜爛，至於此極。

translations.literal: Qishan, when the war had just begun, was the first to show weakness and thereby enervate the army's spirit; the realm was wasted to this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: When the war began Qishan was first to show weakness and sap army morale, and the empire was ruined to this point.

sentences.zh: 既罷斥終身不齒，猶恐不足饜民心而作士氣。

translations.literal: Having been dismissed and excluded for life, one still fears this is not enough to satisfy popular sentiment and revive the spirit of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissal for life should barely satisfy public anger and revive scholarly morale—yet even that seems insufficient.

sentences.zh: 奕經之罪，雖較琦善稍減，文蔚之罪，較奕經又減。

translations.literal: Yijing's crime, though somewhat less than Qishan's, and Wenwei's crime somewhat less than Yijing's,
translations.idiomatic: Yijing's guilt, though somewhat less than Qishan's, and Wenwei's somewhat less than Yijing's,

sentences.zh: 然皇上命將出師，若何慎重。

translations.literal: yet when Your Majesty orders generals to take the field, how grave is the matter.
translations.idiomatic: when Your Majesty sends generals to war, how grave is the trust.

sentences.zh: 奕經頓兵半載，曾未身歷行間，騁其虛憍之氣，自詭一鼓而復三城；

translations.literal: Yijing halted his army half a year, never personally experienced the ranks, gave rein to empty arrogance, and boasted that with one drumbeat he would recover three cities;
translations.idiomatic: Yijing halted his army for half a year without entering the ranks, gave rein to empty arrogance, and boasted he would recover three cities at one stroke;

sentences.zh: 卒之機事不密，貽笑敵人，覆軍殺將，一敗不支。

translations.literal: in the end his plans were not kept secret, he made the enemy laugh, armies were destroyed and generals killed, and one defeat left nothing to support.
translations.idiomatic: in the end his plans leaked, the enemy mocked him, armies were destroyed and generals killed, and one defeat left nothing standing.

sentences.zh: 此不待別科騷擾供億、招權納賄之罪，而已不可勝誅。

translations.literal: this, without counting separate crimes of harassing the people for supplies, usurping power, and taking bribes, is already beyond what punishment can exhaust.
translations.idiomatic: Without even counting crimes of harassing the people, seizing power, and taking bribes, his guilt already exceeds what punishment can exhaust.

sentences.zh: 臣亦知奕經為高宗純皇帝之裔，皇上親親睦族，不忍遽加顯戮。

translations.literal: Your servant also knows Yijing is a descendant of the Gaozong Chun Emperor, and Your Majesty cherishes kin and harmonizes the clan, unwilling to impose sudden execution.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant knows Yijing is a descendant of the Qianlong Emperor and that Your Majesty cherishes the imperial clan and shrinks from executing him outright.

sentences.zh: 然即幸邀寬典，亦當禁錮終身，無為天潢宗室羞，豈圖收禁未及三月，輒复棄瑕錄用？

translations.literal: Yet even if he fortunately receives lenient treatment, he should be confined for life and not bring shame on the imperial clan—how could one imagine that after confinement of less than three months he is again employed, flaws set aside?
translations.idiomatic: Even if he receives mercy, he should be confined for life rather than shame the imperial house—how can he be reappointed after less than three months in confinement?

sentences.zh: 且此數人者，皇上特未知其見惡於民之深耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, regarding these several men, Your Majesty simply does not yet know how deeply they are hated by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty simply does not yet know how deeply the people hate these men.

sentences.zh: 倘俯採輿論，孰不切齒琦善為罪魁，誰不疾首於奕山、奕經、牛鑑、文蔚，而以為投畀之不容緩？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would deign to heed public opinion, who would not gnash his teeth at Qishan as chief culprit, who would not grieve over Yishan, Yijing, Niu Jian, and Wenwei, and regard casting them out as brooking no delay?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty heeded public opinion, who would not gnash his teeth at Qishan as chief culprit, who would not rage at Yishan, Yijing, Niu Jian, and Wenwei, and demand their immediate banishment?

sentences.zh: 此非臣一人之私言也。

translations.literal: This is not your servant's private opinion alone.
translations.idiomatic: This is not your servant's private opinion alone.

sentences.zh: 側聞琦善意侈體汰，跋扈如常，葉爾羌之行，本屬怏怏；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard on the side that Qishan's will is extravagant and his person dissolute, overbearing as before; the journey to Yarkand was from the start resentful;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hears that Qishan remains extravagant and overbearing as before and went to Yarkand unwillingly;

sentences.zh: 今果未及出關，即蒙召還。

translations.literal: now indeed before he had even passed the frontier he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: and now, before he had even left the frontier, he has been recalled.

sentences.zh: 熱河密邇神京，有識無識，莫不撫膺太息，以為皇上鄉用琦善之意，尚不止此。

translations.literal: Rehe is close to the divine capital; the informed and uninformed alike beat their breasts and sigh deeply, thinking Your Majesty's intent to employ Qishan again does not stop here.
translations.idiomatic: Rehe lies close to the capital; learned and common people alike sigh in dismay, fearing Your Majesty intends to employ Qishan for more than this post alone.

sentences.zh: 萬一有事，則熒惑聖聰者，必仍系斯人。

translations.literal: If by chance trouble arises, the one who will mislead the sage hearing will surely still be this man.
translations.idiomatic: If trouble should arise, the man who misleads the throne will surely still be he.

sentences.zh: 履霜堅冰，深可懍懼。

translations.literal: Treading frost leads to solid ice—this is deeply to be feared with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Tread on frost and solid ice follows—a prospect that fills one with dread.

sentences.zh: 頃者禦試翰詹，以'烹阿封即墨'命題，而今茲刑賞顧如此，臣未知皇上所謂阿者何人？

translations.literal: Recently at the imperial examination for Hanlin bachelors the topic was "boiling E and enfeoffing Jimo," yet now punishments and rewards turn out thus; your servant does not know who Your Majesty calls E?
translations.idiomatic: Recently the imperial examination for Hanlin bachelors took "boiling E and enfeoffing Jimo" as its topic, yet punishments and rewards now stand thus; your servant does not know who Your Majesty means by E?

sentences.zh: 即墨者何人？

translations.literal: Who is Jimo?
translations.idiomatic: And who is Jimo?

sentences.zh: 假如聖意高深，偶或差忒，而以即墨為阿，阿為即墨，將毋譽之毀之者有以淆亂是非耶？

translations.literal: If the sage intent is profound and high, and by chance there is some error, and Jimo is taken for E and E for Jimo, will not those who praise and those who slander have means to confuse right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: If the sage intent is profound and there has been some error, and Jimo is taken for E and E for Jimo, will not flatterers and slanderers confuse right and wrong?

sentences.zh: 所望皇上立奮天威，收回成命，體大學絜矩之旨，鑑盈廷毀譽之真，國法稍伸，民心可慰。

translations.literal: What is hoped is that Your Majesty will immediately rouse heavenly authority, withdraw the settled order, embody the aim of the Great Learning in measuring the square, discern the truth of praise and blame filling the court, let state law be somewhat enforced, and popular sentiment may be comforted.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant hopes Your Majesty will rouse imperial authority, withdraw these appointments, heed the Great Learning's teaching on the measuring square, discern true praise and blame in court, enforce the law somewhat, and comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 」疏上，宣宗嘉之，諭曰：「朕無知人之明，以致琦善、奕經、文蔚諸人喪師失律，惟有反躬自責，不欲諉罪臣工。

translations.literal: " When the memorial went up, the Xuanzong Emperor commended it and instructed: "We lack the clarity to know men, so that Qishan, Yijing, Wenwei, and others lost armies and violated discipline; We can only turn and blame Ourselves, and do not wish to shift guilt onto officials.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor commended the memorial and said: "We lacked the discernment to know men, and so Qishan, Yijing, Wenwei, and others lost armies and violated discipline; We can only blame Ourselves and do not wish to shift guilt onto Our officials.

sentences.zh: 今該御史請收回成命，朕非文過飾非之君，豈肯回護？

translations.literal: Now this censor asks to withdraw the settled order; We are not a ruler who covers faults and glosses errors—how would We be willing to shield them?
translations.idiomatic: Now this censor asks to withdraw the appointments; We are not a ruler who covers faults—how would We shield them?

sentences.zh: 」复革琦善等職，令閉門思過。

translations.literal: " He again stripped Qishan and others of office and ordered them to close their doors and reflect on their faults.
translations.idiomatic: " He again stripped Qishan and others of office and ordered them to remain at home and reflect on their faults.

sentences.zh: 於是直聲震海內。

translations.literal: Thereupon his reputation for forthrightness shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for blunt integrity then resounded throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，遷給事中，巡視東城，以事詿吏議，左遷光祿寺署正。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was moved to supervising secretary, inspected the Eastern City, and because of a matter was implicated in official deliberation and demoted to acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he became supervising secretary and inspected the Eastern City, but was implicated in an official inquiry and demoted to acting director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，乞歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he asked to retire home.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，以大學士朱鳳標薦，复授御史，蹶而再起，氣不少撓，疊上疏多關大計。

translations.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor took the throne, on Grand Secretary Zhu Fengbiao's recommendation he was again appointed censor; though he stumbled he rose again, his spirit little diminished, and he submitted memorial after memorial on great state policy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianfeng Emperor took the throne, Grand Secretary Zhu Fengbiao recommended him for censor again; though he had fallen, he rose once more with undiminished spirit and submitted repeated memorials on major state policy.

sentences.zh: 自粵匪起，福建群盜蠢動，蔓延泉、漳、興、永諸郡。

translations.literal: Since the Guangdong rebels arose, bandits in Fujian stirred restlessly and spread through Quan, Zhang, Xing, and Yong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taiping rebellion began, bandits in Fujian stirred and spread through Quan, Zhang, Xing, and Yong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，慶鏞疏陳利害，命回籍治團練。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Qingyong memorialized on advantages and harms and was ordered to return to his native place to organize militia training.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng, Qingyong memorialized on the situation and was ordered home to organize militia.

sentences.zh: 惠安妖婦邱氏煽亂，偵獲置諸法，賜花翎。

translations.literal: The sorceress Qiu of Hui'an incited rebellion; he detected and captured her and had her punished by law, and was granted peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: He detected and punished the sorceress Qiu of Hui'an, who had incited rebellion, and was granted peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 俄以病請開缺。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he asked to vacate his post on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to vacate his post on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 七年，逆匪林俊糾莆陽、仙遊、永春、南安群賊犯泉州，慶鏞激厲士民固守，賊攻圍數日而退。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the rebel Lin Jun gathered bandits from Puyang, Xianyou, Yongchun, and Nan'an to attack Quanzhou; Qingyong roused scholars and commoners to hold firm in defense, and after several days of siege the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the rebel Lin Jun gathered bandits from Puyang, Xianyou, Yongchun, and Nan'an and attacked Quanzhou; Qingyong roused the gentry and people to hold the city, and after several days of siege the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 論功，以道員候選。

translations.literal: When merits were discussed he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒於泉州，贈光祿寺卿，賜祭葬，廕一子知縣，祀鄉賢祠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at Quanzhou, was posthumously granted Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, one son ennobled as district magistrate, and worshipped in the local worthies' shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at Quanzhou, was posthumously made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted state funeral honors, had one son ennobled as district magistrate, and was worshipped in the local worthies' shrine.

sentences.zh: 慶鏞精研漢學​​，而製行則服膺宋儒，文辭樸茂，著有籀經堂文集、三家詩考、說文釋、古籀考等書。

translations.literal: Qingyong deeply studied Han Learning, yet in conduct followed Song Neo-Confucians; his literary style was plain and substantial; he authored the Zhoujing Hall collected works, Examination of the Three Schools' Poetry, Explanation of the Shuowen, Examination of Ancient Zhou Script, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyong was a deep student of Han Learning but in conduct followed Song Neo-Confucians; his prose was plain and solid; he wrote the Zhoujing Hall collected works, Examination of the Three Schools' Poetry, Explanation of the Shuowen, Examination of Ancient Zhou Script, and other works.

sentences.zh: 蘇廷魁，字賡堂，廣東高要人。

translations.literal: Su Tingkui, style name Gengtang, was a native of Gaoyao in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Su Tingkui, whose style was Gengtang, came from Gaoyao in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: A metropolitan graduate of the fifteenth year of Daoguang, selected Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and served as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，遷御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was moved to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became a censor.

sentences.zh: 海疆兵事方亟，迭上疏論列，請修築虎門砲台及燕塘墟、大沙河、龜岡諸要隘，以防敵回擾粵，既而和議成。

translations.literal: Coastal military affairs were pressing; he repeatedly memorialized in series, asking to build fortifications at Humen battery and at Yantangxu, Dashaha, Guigang, and other strategic passes to guard against the enemy returning to harass Guangdong; afterward peace was made.
translations.idiomatic: As coastal war intensified he repeatedly memorialized to build fortifications at Humen and at Yantangxu, Dashaha, Guigang, and other strategic passes to guard against a return of the enemy to Guangdong; peace was made soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 二十三年春，有白氣自天西南隅直掃參旗，因災異上疏數千言，極論時政乖迕，歸罪樞臣穆彰阿等，請立罷黜；

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year a white vapor from the southwestern corner of heaven swept straight through the Shen asterism; because of this omen he memorialized several thousand characters, speaking forcefully on how current policy was at odds, blaming Grand Councillor Mujangga and others, and asking their immediate dismissal;
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the twenty-third year a white vapor swept from the southwestern sky through the Shen asterism; citing this omen he submitted a memorial of several thousand characters denouncing current policy, blaming Grand Councillor Mujangga and others, and demanding their immediate dismissal;

sentences.zh: 並下罪己詔，開直諫之路：語多指斥。

translations.literal: and also issuing an edict of self-blame and opening the path of direct remonstrance—his language was largely accusatory.
translations.idiomatic: he also urged an edict of imperial self-blame and a reopening of direct remonstrance—language largely accusatory in tone.

sentences.zh: 宣宗覽奏動容，嘉其切直，朝野傾望丰采。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor was moved on reading the memorial, commended its blunt directness, and court and countryside looked up to his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor was moved by the memorial, praised its blunt directness, and court and country looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 遭憂去官，服闋，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning, and when mourning ended was moved to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for mourning and, when it ended, became supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，上謹始疏，請求宏濟之道，執勞謙之義，防驕泰之萌，推誠任賢，慎始圖治，選擇翰詹為講官，嚴取孝廉方正備採用，文宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he submitted a memorial on being careful at the beginning, asking to seek the way of great relief, uphold the principle of labor and humility, guard against the sprouting of pride and excess, extend sincerity and employ the worthy, be careful at the start and plan good government, select Hanlin bachelors as lecturers, and strictly choose filial and incorrupt candidates for future use—the Wenzong Emperor commended and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he submitted a memorial on careful beginnings, urging great policies of relief, humility in labor, guarding against pride, sincerity in employing the worthy, careful planning at the start of rule, selection of Hanlin bachelors as lecturers, and strict recruitment of filial and incorrupt candidates—the Xianfeng Emperor commended and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿出督師，援引內閣侍讀穆廕擢五品京堂，在軍機大臣上學習行走。

translations.literal: Saišangga went out to command the army and brought in Grand Secretariat reader-in-waiting Muyin, promoting him to fifth-rank capital official and having him study and serve under the Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: When Saišangga went out to command the army he brought in Grand Secretariat reader Muyin, promoted him to fifth-rank capital official, and had him study under the Grand Councillors.

sentences.zh: 廷魁疏劾其壞舊制，用私親，超擢太驟，易啟幸進之門，請俟賽尚阿還，令回章京本任，詔斥擅預黜陟，猶以素行端方，不之罪。

translations.literal: Tingkui memorialized impeaching him for breaking old regulations, using private kin, promoting too hastily, and easily opening the gate of favor-seeking advancement; he asked that when Saišangga returned Muyin be sent back to his original clerk post. An edict rebuked him for presumptuously interfering in appointments and dismissals, yet because his conduct had always been upright he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Tingkui impeached him for breaking regulations, favoring kin, promoting too hastily, and opening the door to favor-seeking advancement, and asked that Muyin return to his clerk post when Saišangga came back. An edict rebuked Tingkui for interfering in appointments, but because his conduct had always been upright he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 上先隱其名，出疏示賽尚阿，賽尚阿退，飲台垣酒，問：「誰實彈我？

translations.literal: The Emperor first concealed his name and showed the memorial to Saišangga; Saišangga withdrew and drank with the censorate officials, asking: "Who actually impeached me?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor first concealed his name and showed the memorial to Saišangga; Saišangga withdrew and drank with the censorate officials, asking, "Who impeached me?

sentences.zh: 」廷魁出席曰：「公負國，某不敢負公。

translations.literal: " Tingkui rose from his seat and said: "You have failed the state; I dare not fail you.
translations.idiomatic: " Tingkui rose and said, "You have failed the state; I dare not fail you.

sentences.zh: 」再以憂歸。

translations.literal: " He again returned home on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: " He again returned home for mourning.

sentences.zh: 四年，廣東紅巾匪起，將犯省城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Red Turban rebels rose in Guangdong and were about to attack the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Red Turban rebels rose in Guangdong and threatened the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 或獻議借外兵，以鋪捐為餉糈，力爭，罷其議。

translations.literal: Some offered the plan to borrow foreign troops and fund provisions with shop levies; he argued forcefully and had the plan stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed borrowing foreign troops and funding provisions with shop levies; he argued forcefully and had the plan stopped.

sentences.zh: 八年，英法聯軍踞廣州，廷魁與侍郎羅惇衍等倡設團防局，嚴清野，絕漢奸，招募東莞及三元里、佛山練勇得數万人，聲言戒期攻城，敵師出，擊斬百餘級。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Anglo-French allied armies occupied Guangzhou; Tingkui with Vice Minister Luo Dunyan and others initiated a militia defense bureau, strictly cleared the countryside, cut off Chinese collaborators, recruited trained braves from Dongguan, Sanyuanli, and Foshan numbering tens of thousands, announced a set day to attack the city, and when enemy troops came out killed more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Anglo-French forces occupied Guangzhou; Tingkui and Vice Minister Luo Dunyan founded a militia defense bureau, cleared the countryside, cut off collaborators, recruited tens of thousands of braves from Dongguan, Sanyuanli, and Foshan, announced a set day to attack the city, and when enemy troops came out killed more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 敵始有戒心，稍戢，連艘北犯，既而天津議和，廣東敵兵未退，民益憤，廷魁等請留練局以防土寇。

translations.literal: The enemy first grew cautious and somewhat restrained, then sent ships north in succession; afterward peace was made at Tianjin, yet enemy troops in Guangdong did not withdraw and popular anger grew; Tingkui and others asked to retain the militia bureau to guard against local bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy grew cautious and then sent fleets north; peace was made at Tianjin, but foreign troops remained in Guangdong and popular anger grew; Tingkui and others asked to keep the militia bureau against local bandits.

sentences.zh: 敵謂既媾和何復募勇，且以懸金購領事巴夏禮為責言。

translations.literal: The enemy said that since peace had been made why recruit braves again, and also blamed the offering of a bounty for Consul Parkes.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy protested that since peace had been made there was no need to recruit braves, and blamed the bounty placed on Consul Parkes.

sentences.zh: 議和大臣桂良慮撓成議，奏請撤局。

translations.literal: Peace negotiator Guiliang feared this would obstruct the agreement and memorialized to dissolve the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Peace negotiator Guiliang feared this would obstruct the treaty and memorialized to dissolve the bureau.

sentences.zh: 初，艇匪擾廣寧，圍四會、肇慶，兵疲糧罄，或勸之去，廷魁曰：「予團防大臣也，誓與城為存亡！

translations.literal: Earlier, boat bandits harassed Guangning and besieged Sihui and Zhaoqing; troops were weary and grain exhausted; some urged him to leave; Tingkui said: "I am the militia defense commissioner—I swear to live or die with the city!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, boat bandits harassed Guangning and besieged Sihui and Zhaoqing; troops were weary and grain exhausted; some urged him to flee; Tingkui said, "I am the militia defense commissioner—I swear to live or die with the city!

sentences.zh: 」會提督昆壽克梧州，以兵來援，城得完。

translations.literal: " It happened that Provincial Commander Kunshou captured Wuzhou and came with troops to relieve them, and the city was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: " Provincial Commander Kunshou then captured Wuzhou and came with troops to relieve the city, which was saved.

sentences.zh: 疆臣屢欲上其功，皆固辭。

translations.literal: Frontier officials repeatedly wished to report his merit, but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials repeatedly wished to report his merit, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 同治初，以中外大臣薦，授河南開歸陳許道，歷布政使，擢東河總督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, on recommendation of Chinese and foreign great ministers, he was appointed to the Kaifeng circuit of Henan, served as provincial treasurer, and was promoted to Governor-General of the Eastern Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi, on recommendation of Chinese and foreign ministers, he was appointed to the Kaifeng circuit of Henan, served as provincial treasurer, and was promoted to governor-general of the Eastern Rivers.

sentences.zh: 七年，河決滎澤，未奪溜，革職留任，閱三月工竣，復之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the river broke at Xingze without changing course; he was stripped of office but retained in post; after three months the works were completed and he was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the Yellow River broke at Xingze without changing course; he was stripped of rank but kept in post; after three months the works were finished and he was restored.

sentences.zh: 逾年，內召，去官，稱疾歸。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned to the capital, left office, and returned home claiming illness.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was summoned to the capital, left office, and returned home claiming illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 朱琦，字伯韓，廣西臨桂人。

translations.literal: Zhu Qi, style name Bohan, was a native of Lingui in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qi, whose style was Bohan, came from Lingui in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父鳳森，嘉慶六年進士，官河南濬縣知縣，有政聲。

translations.literal: His father Fengsen was a metropolitan graduate of the sixth year of Jiaqing, served as magistrate of Jun County in Henan, and had a reputation for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fengsen earned his jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing, served as magistrate of Jun County in Henan, and was known for good administration.

sentences.zh: 滑縣教匪起，率團練御之，屢破賊，城守卒完。

translations.literal: When sect rebels rose in Hua County he led militia to resist them, repeatedly defeated the bandits, and the city defense was finally preserved.
translations.idiomatic: When sect rebels rose in Hua County he led militia against them, repeatedly defeated the bandits, and preserved the city.

sentences.zh: 遷河南府通判。

translations.literal: He was moved to subprefect of Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to subprefect of Henan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歿，祀名宦。

translations.literal: He died and was worshipped in the shrine of famous officials.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was worshipped in the shrine of famous officials.

sentences.zh: 琦，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Qi placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Qi placed first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and served as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 慕同里陳宏謀之為人，以氣節自勵。

translations.literal: He admired the character of his fellow townsman Chen Hongmou and urged himself on with moral integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He admired his fellow townsman Chen Hongmou and urged himself on with moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，值海疆事定，禍機四伏，而上下復習委靡，言路多容默，深以為憂。

translations.literal: He was moved to censor; it happened that coastal affairs were settled, yet peril lurked on every side while above and below again fell into lax weakness and the avenue of speech was largely silent—he was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He became a censor just as coastal affairs were settled, yet peril lurked everywhere while court and country relapsed into lax weakness and remonstrance fell largely silent—he was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 著名實說，略曰：「天下有鄉曲之行，有大人之行。

translations.literal: He wrote Discourse on Names and Reality, which in summary says: "Under Heaven there is the conduct of village circles and the conduct of great men.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Discourse on Names and Reality, which in summary says: "Under Heaven there is the conduct of village circles and the conduct of great men.

sentences.zh: 鄉曲、大人，其名也，考之其行，而察其有用與否，其實也。

translations.literal: Village circles and great men are names; examining their conduct and observing whether they are useful or not—that is the reality.
translations.idiomatic: Village circles and great men are names; examining conduct and observing whether it is useful—that is reality.

sentences.zh: 世之稱者，曰謹厚，曰廉靜，日退讓，三者名之至美也，而不知此鄉曲之行也，非所謂大人者也。

translations.literal: What the age praises are called cautious and substantial, called pure and quiet, called daily yielding—these three are names of utmost beauty, yet one does not know that this is the conduct of village circles, not what are called great men.
translations.idiomatic: What the age praises as cautious and substantial, pure and quiet, and daily yielding are names of utmost beauty, yet these are the conduct of village circles, not what are called great men.

sentences.zh: 大人之職，在於經國家、安社稷，有剛毅之大節，為人主畏憚；

translations.literal: The duty of great men lies in ordering the state and securing the altars of soil and grain; they have great integrity of firm resolve and are feared and respected by the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: The duty of great men is to order the state and secure the realm; they have great integrity of firm resolve and are feared and respected by the ruler;

sentences.zh: 有深謀遠慮，為天下長計。

translations.literal: they have deep plans and far-reaching thought and make long-term plans for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: they have deep plans and far-reaching thought and make long-term plans for the empire.

sentences.zh: 合則留，不合以義去。

translations.literal: If in accord they stay; if not in accord they leave according to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: If in accord they stay; if not in accord they leave on principle.

sentences.zh: 身之便安，不暇計也；

translations.literal: Their own ease and comfort they have no leisure to calculate;
translations.idiomatic: They have no leisure to calculate their own ease and comfort;

sentences.zh: 世之指摘，不敢逃也。

translations.literal: the world's blame they dare not flee.
translations.idiomatic: and they dare not flee the world's blame.

sentences.zh: 今也不然。

translations.literal: Today it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is not so.

sentences.zh: 曰：吾為天下長計，則天下之釁必集於我；

translations.literal: They say: If I make long-term plans for all under Heaven, then the troubles of all under Heaven will surely gather on me;
translations.idiomatic: They say: If I make long-term plans for the empire, trouble will gather on me;

sentences.zh: 吾為人主畏憚，則不能久於其位；

translations.literal: if I am feared and respected by the ruler, I cannot long remain in my post;
translations.idiomatic: if I am feared and respected by the ruler, I cannot long keep my post;

sentences.zh: 不如謹厚、廉靜、退讓，此三者可以安坐而無患，而名又至美也。

translations.literal: better to be cautious and substantial, pure and quiet, and yielding—these three allow one to sit at ease without trouble, and the name is again of utmost beauty.
translations.idiomatic: better to be cautious and substantial, pure and quiet, and yielding—these three let one sit at ease without trouble and win the finest reputation.

sentences.zh: 夫無患而可久於其位，又有天下美名，士何憚而不爭趨於此？

translations.literal: To be without trouble and able to long remain in one's post, and also have the world's finest name—what would scholars shrink from in not scrambling toward this?
translations.idiomatic: What scholar would not scramble toward a post without trouble, long tenure, and the world's finest name?

sentences.zh: 故近世所稱公卿之賢者，此三者為多矣。

translations.literal: Therefore among those called worthy among ministers and grandees in recent times, these three are the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Thus most of those called worthy among recent ministers and grandees possess these three traits.

sentences.zh: 當其瓘冠襜裾，從容正步，趨於廊廟之間，上之人不疑，而非議不加，其沉深不可測也。

translations.literal: When they wear jade caps and long robes, walk with easy upright steps, and hasten between palace corridors, those above do not doubt them and no censure is added; they seem deep and immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing jade caps and court robes, walking with easy upright steps through palace corridors, they seem above doubt and beyond censure—deep and immeasurable.

sentences.zh: 一旦遇大利害，搶攘無措，鉗口撟舌而莫敢言，而所謂謹厚、廉靜、退讓，至此舉無可用，於是始思向之為人主畏憚而有深謀遠慮者，不可得矣。

translations.literal: Once they meet great advantage and harm, they are flustered without resource, clamp their mouths and twist their tongues and dare not speak; and the so-called cautious and substantial, pure and quiet, and yielding—at this point none can be used. Then one begins to think of those formerly feared and respected by the ruler and possessing deep plans and far-reaching thought—they cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: But when great crisis comes they are flustered and helpless, clamp their mouths and dare not speak, and cautiousness, purity, and yielding prove useless; only then do they realize that men once feared by the ruler and possessed of deep foresight are nowhere to be found.

sentences.zh: 且謹厚、廉靜、退讓三者，非果無用也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the three—cautious and substantial, pure and quiet, and yielding—are not truly without use.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, cautiousness, purity, and yielding are not truly without use.

sentences.zh: 古有負蓋世之功而思持其後，挾震主之威而唯恐不終，未嘗不斤斤於此，故又於鎮薄俗、保晚節。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were those who bore world-surpassing merit and thought to preserve their legacy, or wielded awe-inspiring power over the ruler and feared they would not end well—they never failed to be scrupulous in these matters, and therefore also used them to restrain shallow custom and preserve integrity in later years.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity men who bore world-surpassing merit or wielded awe-inspiring power over the ruler were scrupulous in these matters to preserve their legacy and restrain shallow custom in their later years.

sentences.zh: 後世無其才而冒其位，安其樂而避其患，假於名之至美，僴然自以為足。

translations.literal: Later generations, without such talent yet usurping such posts, enjoying their pleasure and avoiding their troubles, borrow the utmost beauty of the name and complacently think themselves sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations, without such talent yet holding such posts, enjoy their pleasure, avoid trouble, borrow the finest names, and complacently think themselves sufficient.

sentences.zh: 是藏身之固，莫便此三者。

translations.literal: As a secure place to hide the body, nothing is more convenient than these three.
translations.idiomatic: As a secure place to hide, nothing is more convenient than these three.

sentences.zh: 孔子之所謂鄙夫也，其究鄉愿也。

translations.literal: They are what Confucius called petty men; in the end they are village worthies.
translations.idiomatic: They are what Confucius called petty men—in the end, village worthies.

sentences.zh: 是張禹、胡廣、趙戒之類也，甚矣其恥也！

translations.literal: They are of the sort of Zhang Yu, Hu Guang, and Zhao Jie—how great is the shame!
translations.idiomatic: They are men of the sort of Zhang Yu, Hu Guang, and Zhao Jie—how shameful!

sentences.zh: 」於是數上疏切論時務，皆留中不報。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he repeatedly submitted memorials speaking forcefully on current affairs, all retained in the palace and not answered.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted repeated memorials on urgent affairs of state, all retained in the palace without response.

sentences.zh: 時咸推其抗直，稱為名御史。

translations.literal: At the time all praised his forthright resistance and called him a famous censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all praised his blunt integrity and called him a famous censor.

sentences.zh: 琦以言既不見用，二十六年，告歸。

translations.literal: Because Qi's words were not employed, in the twenty-sixth year he asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When his advice went unheeded, he asked to retire home in the twenty-sixth year.

sentences.zh: 越數年，廣西群賊蜂起，其言皆驗。

translations.literal: After several years bandits rose in swarms in Guangxi, and all his words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years bandits rose throughout Guangxi, and all his warnings proved true.

sentences.zh: 家居治團練，助守禦。

translations.literal: At home he organized militia training and assisted in defense.
translations.idiomatic: At home he organized militia and assisted in defense.

sentences.zh: 賊中梟傑張家祥者，悔罪投誠，當事猶疑之。

translations.literal: Among the bandits the chieftain Zhang Jiaxiang repented his crimes and submitted in good faith, yet those in charge still doubted him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit chieftain Zhang Jiaxiang repented and submitted, yet officials still doubted him.

sentences.zh: 琦知其忠勇可用，以全家保之，乃受降，改名國樑，卒為名將。

translations.literal: Qi knew his loyalty and courage could be used, guaranteed him with his whole family, then accepted his surrender; he was renamed Guoliang and in the end became a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Qi saw that his loyalty and courage could be used, pledged his own family as guarantee, accepted his surrender, renamed him Guoliang, and he became a famous general.

sentences.zh: 琦以守城勞議敘，以道員候選。

translations.literal: For his labor in defending the city merits were discussed and he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: For defending the city he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 咸豐六年，再至京師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he again reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 居兩歲，從欽差大臣桂良至江蘇，無所遇，王有齡獨重之，有齡撫浙，闢贊軍事。

translations.literal: After two years he followed Imperial Commissioner Guiliang to Jiangsu, met with no success, but Wang Youling alone valued him; when Youling became governor of Zhejiang he was appointed to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he followed Imperial Commissioner Guiliang to Jiangsu without success, but Wang Youling valued him; when Youling became governor of Zhejiang he appointed Qi to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一年，粵匪犯杭州，總理團練局。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Guangdong rebels attacked Hangzhou; he directed the militia training bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Taiping rebels attacked Hangzhou, and he directed the militia bureau.

sentences.zh: 守清波門，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: He defended the Qingbo Gate; when the city fell he died there.
translations.idiomatic: He defended the Qingbo Gate and died when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 贈太常寺卿，予騎都尉世職，祀昭忠祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, given the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant, and worshipped in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted a hereditary Cavalry Commandant rank, and worshipped in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 琦學宗程、朱，詩古文皆有法，著有怡志堂集、台垣奏議。

translations.literal: Qi's learning followed the Cheng and Zhu school; his poetry and ancient prose all had method; he authored the Yizhi Hall collected works and Censorate memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's learning followed the Cheng-Zhu school; his poetry and prose were disciplined; he wrote the Yizhi Hall collected works and Censorate memorials.

sentences.zh: 論曰：禁煙之議，創自黃爵滋，行之操切，而邊釁遂開，繼之游移而國威愈墮，誠不可以此歸咎始議之人。

translations.literal: The commentary says: The proposal to prohibit opium was initiated by Huang Juezi; carried out with harsh urgency, border hostilities thus opened; followed by vacillation and national prestige fell further—truly one cannot blame this on those who first proposed it.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: The drive to prohibit opium began with Huang Juezi; carried out harshly, it opened border war; followed by vacillation, national prestige fell further—yet one cannot blame those who first proposed it.

sentences.zh: 然謀國萬全，決胜千里，非恃意氣為也。

translations.literal: Yet to plan for the state's complete security and decide victory a thousand li away does not rely on spirit and ardor alone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet planning for the state's complete security and deciding victory a thousand li away cannot rely on spirit alone.

sentences.zh: 行固維艱，言亦豈易易哉？

translations.literal: Action is inherently difficult to sustain—how could speech be easy?
translations.idiomatic: Action is hard to sustain—how much harder is speech?

sentences.zh: 金應麟同被拔擢，亦始終主戰。

translations.literal: Jin Yinglin was likewise specially promoted and also consistently advocated war.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yinglin was likewise promoted and also consistently favored war.

sentences.zh: 陳慶鏞、蘇廷魁、朱琦時稱「三直」；

translations.literal: Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi were at the time called the "Three Upright Ones";
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi were called the "Three Upright Ones";

sentences.zh: 合之應麟，又稱「四虎」。

translations.literal: adding Yinglin, they were also called the "Four Tigers."
translations.idiomatic: with Yinglin added, the "Four Tigers."

sentences.zh: 所言有用有不用，凜凜然有生氣，要足以砭頑振懦矣。

translations.literal: What they said was sometimes used and sometimes not, yet stern and vital with living spirit—enough, in sum, to pierce the stubborn and rouse the timid.
translations.idiomatic: Their words were sometimes heeded and sometimes not, yet stern and vital—enough, in the end, to pierce stubbornness and rouse the timid.
